displayName: Panoptent — Click & Edit with Claude Code
description: Click any element in your running app, say what to change — Claude Code edits the source. Visual editing for VS Code and Chrome.
config.language: Language of the Panoptent interface: preview panel, page overlay, Chrome extension, notifications and the prompts sent to Claude. Quick switch: [Panoptent: Change Language](command:panoptent.changeLanguage).
config.language.auto: Follow VS Code's display language (English if not supported)
config.defaultUrl: Dev server address suggested when you open the preview, e.g. `http://localhost:5173`. Each project remembers the last address you used.
config.previewIn: Where the page opens when you start Panoptent. VS Code's **Integrated Browser** (1.109+) has real cookies, logins and DevTools; with the same in-page bar and drawer as the Chrome extension.
config.previewIn.auto: Integrated Browser if this VS Code has it, otherwise inside the Panoptent panel
config.previewIn.browser: Always open the page in VS Code's Integrated Browser
config.previewIn.panel: Show the page inside the Panoptent panel (classic preview)
config.openSourceOnSelect: When you select an element, open its source file at the matching line, without taking focus from the preview.
config.sendTo: Where your changes go when you press **Apply**.
config.sendTo.claudePanel: Hands the request to the Claude Code panel in VS Code, prefilled; you press Enter.
config.sendTo.cli: Runs the Claude Code CLI in the background; progress shows in the Panoptent panel. Configure it under *Background mode (CLI)* below.
config.sendTo.mcp: Claude Code fetches the changes itself from the Panoptent MCP server: Apply copies a one-line command instead of attaching a request file (or type /mcp__panoptent__apply_queue in Claude Code). Panoptent offers to connect Claude Code the first time.
config.designFile:
Design rules file Claude should follow for UI changes, relative to the project folder (e.g. `design.md`).

- *Empty*: automatic, uses `design.md`, `DESIGN.md` or `docs/design.md` if present
- `off`: disabled

Easiest to pick with [Panoptent: Choose Design Rules File](command:panoptent.chooseDesignFile).
config.claudePath:
Claude Code CLI command or full path. If `claude` is not on your PATH, the CLI bundled with the Claude Code extension is used.

The settings in this section apply only when [Send To](#panoptent.sendTo#) is *In the background (CLI)*.
config.permissionMode: What Claude Code may do without asking while it runs in the background.
config.permissionMode.acceptEdits: Recommended. Allows file edits, rejects other terminal commands.
config.permissionMode.default: Claude Code default: anything that needs permission is rejected, since nobody can answer in the background.
config.permissionMode.plan: Plan only; no files are changed.
config.permissionMode.auto: Claude Code decides what is safe to run on its own.
config.permissionMode.bypassPermissions: Allows everything, including terminal commands, without asking. Use with care.
config.model: Model to use, e.g. `sonnet` or `opus`. Leave empty for the Claude Code default.
config.reloadAfterEdit: Fully reload the preview when Claude finishes. Not needed for projects with hot reload (Vite, Next, Nuxt).
config.chromeBridge: Let the Chrome extension connect to this VS Code window. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only and asks for your approval the first time a browser connects.
config.bridgePort: First port the Chrome bridge tries; if it is taken, the next 9 ports are tried.
config.mcpServer: Run a local MCP server (127.0.0.1 only) so AI agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Windsurf can read the selected elements, the queue and the page context, and mark changes as applied. Connect Claude Code with [Panoptent: Connect Claude Code (MCP)](command:panoptent.connectClaudeCode).
config.mcpPort: First port the MCP server tries; if it is taken, the next 9 ports are tried. The address is `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/mcp`.
view.home.welcome:
Preview your app, click an element, say what to change — Claude Code edits the code.
[$(eye) Open Preview](command:panoptent.open)
Start your dev server first (e.g. npm run dev).
Link elements to their exact file and line so Claude doesn't spend time and tokens searching: [set up code-inspector automatically](command:panoptent.setupCodeInspector) · [setup guide](command:panoptent.setupGuide)
